page: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2.0 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes a 50 MB L3 cache, a 524 GB local SSD, and support for Premium Storage. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1245.79, while the multi-core execution reached 6562.94. Memory bandwidth tests showed average throughput, with cached small-block reads at 366.56 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 49.76 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations both performed in the average tier, with Redis achieving 6.41 million operations per second. However, tasks like static web serving at 6.16 GB/sec and LLM text generation on a 7B model at 4.85 tokens/sec fell into the weak and poor categories respectively.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per core, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute scaling. The combination of 256.0 GB of RAM and a 524 GB local SSD makes it suitable for hosting relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. It is less suitable for compute-bound tasks, high-throughput web serving, or large-scale machine learning inference due to its lower single-core and multi-threaded processing benchmarks.
